Predicates:
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
LocatedIn(x, y) ::: x is located in y.
Island(x) ::: x is an island.
Place(x) ::: x is a place.
SouthShetlandIslands(x) ::: x is the South Shetland Islands.
Antarctica(x) ::: x is Antarctica.
LocatedInTransitive(x, y) ::: if x is located in y, and y is in z, then x is in z.
Question:
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Barutin Cove is named after all islands in Antarctica.
Predicates:
NamedAfter(barutinCove, y) ::: Barutin Cove is named after y.
Island(y) ::: y is an island.
LocatedIn(barutinCove, snowIsland) ::: Barutin Cove is located in Snow Island.
LocatedIn(snowIsland, southShetlandIslands) ::: Snow Island is located in the South Shetland Islands.
LocatedIn(southShetlandIslands, antarctica) ::: The South Shetland Islands are located in Antarctica.
LocatedInTransitive(barutinCove, antarctica) ::: If Barutin Cove is in Snow Island and Snow Island is in South Shetland Islands, and South Shetland Islands are in Antarctica, then Barutin Cove is in Antarctica.
Premises:
LocatedIn(barutinCove, snowIsland) ∧ LocatedIn(snowIsland, southShetlandIslands) ∧ LocatedIn(southShetlandIslands, antarctica) ::: Barutin Cove is on Snow Island, which is in the South Shetland Islands, which are in Antarctica.
Conclusion:
∀y (Island(y) ∧ NamedAfter(barutinCove, y)) → y ∈ Antarctica ::: For all y, if y is an island and Barutin Cove is named after y, then y is in Antarctica.
